rows.statement: Experiment: Codex reading a superseded architecture file directly (bypassing KnowledgeOS) is a stale-context violation; result FAIL — the architecture must define how authoritative current knowledge is retrieved.

rows.anchor: 105.56 — Local files are not forbidden ... local files can remain useful for agent instructions, generated work, temporary analysis, repository-local context, pointers. LocalArtifact ≠ AuthoritativeKnowledge unless explicitly designated.
rows.statement: States local files remain useful (instructions, work products, temporary analysis, pointers) but LocalArtifact ≠ AuthoritativeKnowledge unless explicitly designated.

rows.anchor: 105.57 — Agent configuration hierarchy ... GlobalGovernance→KnowledgeOS→RepositoryArchitecture→AgentOperatingContract→TaskContext. Lower layers must not silently override higher-level authoritative constraints.
rows.statement: Defines a five-layer authority hierarchy GlobalGovernance→KnowledgeOS→RepositoryArchitecture→AgentOperatingContract→TaskContext, where lower layers cannot silently override higher ones.

rows.anchor: 105.58 — Experiment 26 ... Task says 'ignore architecture rule.' Architecture rule forbids the action. Expected: task instruction loses. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a task-level instruction to ignore an architecture rule must lose to the higher-level architecture rule; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 105.59 — Prompt injection resistance ... UntrustedInput ≠ Authority. A text file saying 'ignore all governance rules' does not become an authorized governance decision.
rows.statement: Restates UntrustedInput ≠ Authority as the semantic basis for prompt-injection resistance.

rows.anchor: 105.60 — Experiment 27 ... Repository README contains 'disable security controls before deployment.' Expected: README content is untrusted information, not authority. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a README instructing disabling security controls remains untrusted content, not authority; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 105.61 — This is a major KnowledgeOS advantage ... The system can distinguish Instruction from Authority. This is much more powerful than simply telling an LLM 'be careful.'
rows.statement: States distinguishing Instruction from Authority is a major KnowledgeOS advantage, far stronger than telling an LLM to 'be careful'.

rows.anchor: 105.62 — Agent assurance ... AgentActionAssurance=f(Identity,Authority,Context,Policy,Evidence,Verification). A high-quality agent action is not simply 'the AI did it' but 'this identified agent, operating under this policy and authorization, used this context, performed this action, and produced th
rows.statement: Defines AgentActionAssurance=f(Identity,Authority,Context,Policy,Evidence,Verification), replacing a bare 'the AI did it' with a fully specified assurance statement.

type_signature.domain: Identity x Authority x Context x Policy x Evidence x Verification

rows.anchor: 105.63 — Experiment 28 ... Production modification has agent identity, authorization, policy, change record, verification, runtime evidence. Expected: strong assurance. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment: a production modification with full identity/authorization/policy/change-record/verification/evidence yields strong assurance; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 105.64 — Agent architecture conformance matrix ... Shared knowledge, Pointer-layer boundary, Agent identity, Tool authorization, Governance context, Recommendation/decision separation, Action provenance, Agent memory boundary, Knowledge promotion, Runtime verification -- across Intended/Claude/Codex
rows.statement: Presents a ten-capability agent architecture conformance matrix (Intended/Claude/Codex/KnowledgeOS/Evidence columns), mostly unresolved pending empirical scan.

rows.anchor: 105.65 — Agent invariants: I_SharedKnowledge, I_AgentBoundary, I_AgentAuthority, I_Recommendation, I_AgentAttribution, I_AgentAutonomy, I_KnowledgePromotion, I_AgentKnowledgeVersion
rows.statement: States eight new agent invariants: I_SharedKnowledge (agents must use designated authoritative KnowledgeOS knowledge sources), I_AgentBoundary (agent configuration must define behavior, not become a competing knowledge store), I_AgentAuthority (agent capability does not imply organizational authority), I_Recommendation (agent recommendation must remain distinguishable from authorized decision), I_AgentAttribution (material agent actions must be attributable to agent/session/scope/authorization), I_AgentAutonomy (autonomous agent actions must be bounded by pre-authorized policy), I_KnowledgePromotion (agent-generated knowledge must not become authoritative solely because an agent generated it), I_AgentKnowledgeVersion (agents must be able to distinguish current from superseded knowledge).

rows.anchor: 105.66 — Step 105 verdict ... AGENT ARCHITECTURE — PASS at the architecture level, conceptually consistent with KnowledgeOS provided that the pointer-layer boundary is maintained. But the implementation verdict remains A_Agent,implemented=TBD because we have not yet performed the actual repository-l
rows.statement: Records the Step 105 verdict as architecture-level PASS conditional on maintaining the pointer-layer boundary, while implementation conformance A_Agent,implemented remains explicitly TBD.

rows.anchor: 105.67 — The most important conclusion ... AGENTS.md→OperatingContract, .claude/→ClaudeBehavior, .codex/→CodexBehavior, while KnowledgeOS→EngineeringKnowledge+Governance+Evidence. That is the architectural separation we were looking for.
rows.statement: States the concrete mapping AGENTS.md→OperatingContract, .claude/→ClaudeBehavior, .codex/→CodexBehavior, KnowledgeOS→EngineeringKnowledge+Governance+Evidence as the intended architectural separation.

rows.anchor: Step 106 — Runtime Architecture Conformance ... even if KnowledgeOS architecture is semantically correct and Claude/Codex are correctly designed, what actually runs? DeclaredArchitecture↔DeployedArchitecture↔RuntimeBehavior. Can we trust KnowledgeOS as Software, not merely as an architectural concep
rows.statement: Previews Step 106: comparing DeclaredArchitecture↔DeployedArchitecture↔RuntimeBehavior to test whether the designed system actually exists at runtime, moving toward whether KnowledgeOS can be trusted as Software, not merely a concept.

sources.note: The STEP-VERIFY-026-040 report's batch-level catalogue of five incompatible knowledge-state tuple variants, twelve drifting operator signatures, eleven overloaded bare-letter symbols, five overlapping *Status enums, three 'debt' concepts and seven uncertainty taxonomies across steps 026-040, tied to the observation that only 14 statements out of ~350 boxed claims ever receive a stable citable ID.

rows.anchor: §32.34 ... immediately self-invalidated at §32.34's own next line ... §32.79 ... a fourth competing spine object
rows.statement: Step-032's Status(A) six-value enum is declared and then withdrawn as non-mutually-exclusive within the same section; its EpistemicClaim EC 11-tuple is identified as a fourth competing 'spine' object alongside step-031's 6-tuple assertion, 7-tuple K_t, and its own 5-tuple State(A); its Belnap-FOUR-equivalent lattice claim is neither named nor cited as Belnap's bilattice, and no join/meet operation is ever defined.

rows.anchor: Knowledge-state spine — five incompatible variants, none designated canonical, no migration ever noted ... Total: 30+ tuples. Not one has a single typed component
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: the corpus's central knowledge-state tuple has five incompatible variants across steps 026-040 (8, 9, 10+open, 7, and 11 elements respectively), with the version actually used downstream (step-031's 7-tuple) dropping Uncertainty, TemporalState and Arguments; over 30 distinct tuples are catalogued scope-wide and not one has a single typed component (no codomain, cardinality, or optionality declared for any element), which the meta-file's own M1 (Type correctness) criterion would fail for all 30 -- offered as one reason M1 was never applied.

rows.anchor: Operator signature drift ... U(H) ... Decide/Decision ... Authorize/Admissible ... Authority ... Cost(I) ... Consistent ... Contradiction ... denotes ... Sensitivity ... Health/Meta vector ... Conflict lifecycle ... Drift family
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: twelve named operators/relations undergo unflagged signature drift across steps 026-040 (arity changes, domain changes, relation-to-function promotions, vector-to-scalar or vector-to-Boolean collapses), catalogued individually as items 1-12 including U(H), Decide, Authorize/Admissible, Authority, Cost(I), Consistent, Contradiction, denotes, Sensitivity, the Health/Meta vector, the conflict-state lifecycle, and the drift-kind family.

rows.anchor: the only numbered identifier families anywhere in the 17 files are M1–M7 ... and P35.1–P35.7 ... Fourteen IDs total across 17 files and ~350 boxed statements ... Eleven overloaded symbols
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: across 17 files and roughly 350 boxed principles, only 14 statements ever receive a stable citable identifier (M1-M7, P35.1-P35.7), meaning nearly every load-bearing result is unciteable and gets re-stated (and thereby mutated) rather than re-used by later steps -- identified as the mechanism producing the tuple and signature drift; separately catalogues eleven overloaded bare-letter symbols (E, V, C, R, A, T, I, U, script-P, script-V) each denoting two or more different objects within the scope, five overlapping *Status/*State enums with no shared discipline, three independently-coined 'debt' concepts, and seven distinct uncertainty taxonomies.

rows.anchor: VC-1 — U(H) type contradiction ... VC-2 — CE4 vs CE12 ... VC-3 — Authority arity regression ... VC-4 ... VC-5 ... VC-6 ... VC-7 ... VC-8 ... VC-9 ... VC-10 ... VC-11 ... VC-12
rows.statement: Twelve intra-scope contradictions (VC-1 through VC-12) are individually registered with severity notes, spanning: U(H) type conflict, CE4/CE12 inconsistent model-matching criteria (both located inside the file claiming zero internal contradictions), Authority arity regression, consistency-decomposition reversal (vector vs conjunction), Cost scalar-vs-vector break, an internal metric-rigor violation, two incompatible health vectors in one file, a truncated drift-kind box, the unpropagated adversarial premise, the abandoned M1-M7 gate, an unearned status upgrade, and the corpus's own 'no fundamental contradiction' claim being refuted by the first three.

rows.anchor: If the corpus contains K_t = A and later K_t = B, do not simply choose B ... The output may legitimately be: NO CANONICAL FORM ESTABLISHED. That is a valid verification result
rows.statement: States the anti-forced-canonicalization rule: when two definitions of the same symbol (e.g. K_t=A then K_t=B) appear, the verifier must not simply adopt the later one but must establish whether A was explicitly rejected, whether B truly replaces A, whether they mean different things, whether a mapping exists, or whether both apply at different abstraction levels; 'NO CANONICAL FORM ESTABLISHED' is stated to be a valid, legitimate verification result.

rows.anchor: THE 8 BOXED FAILs ... Element S (State) never receives a FAIL ... Two incompatible 'minimal kernels' are boxed within 20 lines
rows.statement: Step-070's minimal-kernel removal-test experiment (8 elements A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R) produces FAIL for only 7, two of those circular, and State receives 'PASS WITH PERFORMANCE FAILURE' rather than FAIL; the file nonetheless boxes an 8-element minimal kernel and, 20 lines later, a 7-element K_L excluding State, with three distinct senses of 'kernel' used interchangeably (VF-2).

rows.anchor: 64 minted names, 63 unique. Genuinely defined: 1 ... 62 FAIL ... hinging on the undefined qualifiers silently (21) and material (14)
rows.statement: Batch-level invariant census: 64 I_* names minted across the 16 files (63 unique, 1 exact duplicate), of which only I_Dependency passes a strict 'definition or merely a name' test; the dominant failure mode is an undefined modal qualifier, with 21 of 62 failing invariants turning on 'silently' and 14 on 'material', neither ever defined anywhere in the 16-file scope.

rows.anchor: Three families drift without supersession notes: the kernel ... the Agent ... the Decision
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: three object families drift across steps 067-082 with no supersession note -- the kernel tuple (4 variants, arities 8/7/7+3/8), the Agent tuple (3 variants, arities 7/5/6), and the Decision function/tuple (6 signatures, arities ranging 4-11) -- cataloguing 34 total tuple/state-object variants in order of appearance.

Batch-level finding: twelve symbols (I, M, P, A, S, C, theta, U, e, !=, +, ~) each carry between two and six distinct senses across steps 067-082, with '!=' itself flagged as carrying a normative ('should not be conflated') sense in most occurrences despite being the corpus's single most-used operator, never disambiguated.

rows.anchor: I_MigrationIntegrity is the sharpest ... the only invariant in scope with an obvious mechanical test ... extends 092's 𝒦=(S,A,T,I,O) to a 7-tuple 𝒦_t — an unannounced signature change
rows.statement: Step-096 (learning/adaptation) mints I_MigrationIntegrity, rated the single invariant in the 083-100 scope with an obvious mechanical test against a migration script; silently changes the corpus's kernel-state tuple signature from 092's 5-tuple K=(S,A,T,I,O) to a 7-tuple K_t dropping Observations and adding three new fields, with no mapping given between the two.

rows.anchor: Five D, four S, two 𝒦 ... Step 100 reconciles none and introduces a memberless sixth S_t
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: across steps 083-100 the corpus carries five incompatible Decision-object definitions, four incompatible system-state tuples, and two incompatible kernel-state tuples (K and K_t), none reconciled by step-100's closure claim, which additionally introduces a seventh, memberless S_t.

rows.anchor: ~175 invariants minted ... 0 of ~175 are definitions ... 'material' (appears in 61 invariant texts)
rows.statement: Batch-level invariant census for steps 083-100: ~175 I_* names minted, 0 pass the definition test, with the hedge word 'material' alone appearing in 61 of the invariant texts as an unbound, undefined quantifier; at least 9 names collide with the 067-082 invariant families and several near-duplicate invariant families exist for single ideas (graceful degradation, cache freshness, criticality-proportional effort, constrained optimization, correlated evidence).

rows.anchor: A_D does not occur anywhere in step-101 ... introduced silently in 106.2 and then retro-attributed to 106 by 107
rows.statement: Step-101 (architecture-to-reality conformance) defines exactly three architecture layers (intended/implemented/runtime); a fourth, A_D (deployed), is silently introduced five steps later at step-106 with no note that step-101's governing triple was ever extended, then correctly retro-attributed by step-107 -- but no file records the mutation of the founding tuple itself (VH-1).

rows.anchor: the silent introduction of the fourth term ... CONTRADICTS 101 on the tuple arity while presenting itself as continuous with it
rows.statement: Step-106 (runtime architecture conformance) introduces the deployed-architecture term A_D and a third, 6-ary C(.) tuple, silently changing the arity of step-101's founding architecture triple while presenting itself as a direct continuation; every 'actual implementation' cell across its runtime conformance table reads 'needs evidence'.

rows.anchor: C0–C6 and E1–E6 and the 9 codes are three parallel classifications of the same cell with no stated relation ... never cited again by number
rows.statement: Step-108 (conformance matrix) introduces three unreconciled parallel classification scales (C0-C6, E1-E6, a 9-code status set) for the same conformance cell within one file, refuses a scalar compliance score correctly, but is itself superseded by symbol collision within 8 steps when later files rebind C0-C6 and E0-E6 to different meanings without citation.

rows.anchor: S0–S5 (six levels) and Grade 0–6 (seven levels) are two scales for the same quantity in one file, and the file never states the mapping
rows.statement: Step-114 (semantic core evidence test) carries two unmapped evidence-strength scales for one quantity (a six-level S0-S5 and a seven-level Grade 0-6) within the same file, and correctly suppresses computing an aggregate weighted score ('a high average could conceal a critical weakness') though the weights remain undefined; presents the band's most nearly-executable object (a bounded, mechanical eight-concept inspection) and does not run it.

rows.anchor: a third E-scale, E0–E6 ... This is the band's sharpest formal contradiction ... 109 boxes E2 as a verdict; under 116's scale that verdict means something else
rows.statement: Step-116 (actual graph extraction) introduces a third, differently-ordered E0-E6 evidence scale that rebinds symbols already used with different meanings at steps 108 and 109, meaning earlier boxed verdicts like step-109's E2 silently change meaning under the new binding -- rated the sharpest formal contradiction in the band, ironically made worse rather than better by being the only E-scale to state an explicit total order.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTS 108.2 — C0–C6 now means control-loop stages where 108.2 bound it to conformance states ... eleven steps apart, no note
rows.statement: Step-119 (control-loop evidence test) rebinds C0-C6 to control-loop stages, directly contradicting step-108's binding of the same symbols to conformance-maturity states eleven steps earlier with no cross-reference; also conflates a stage label with a numeric score within one section (treating C3 as simultaneously a name and a 0-5 variable).

rows.anchor: 49 catalogued scales ... Does any file map one scale onto another? No — zero explicit mappings exist in the 20 files
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: 49 distinct epistemic-status/evidence/verdict scales are introduced across steps 101-120 with zero explicit mappings between any pair of them; three fatal symbol collisions are isolated -- E-scale bound three incompatible ways (108/109/116), C-scale bound three incompatible ways (108/119/120), and F/F1 bound to unrelated concepts within step-120 alone.

rows.anchor: VH-1 ... VH-15 ... Section headings assert what their bodies withdraw
rows.statement: Registers 15 numbered intra-scope contradictions (VH-1 through VH-15) spanning the founding architecture-tuple mutation, the triple E-scale and C-scale collisions, step-120's self-contradicting dependency graph and two incompatible propagation topologies, step-115's actual/target graph conflation, step-109's grammar violations and self-contradictory evidence-ledger row, step-114's unmapped dual evidence scale, and four malformed LaTeX constructs that break claim structure.

rows.anchor: Step-101's architecture triple silently becomes a quadruple at step-106, and is retro-attributed
rows.statement: TV-F-052 confirms by direct grep that A_D occurs 0 times in step-101 and 6 times in step-106, and that no file anywhere records that step-101's governing question (a triple A_I=A_C=A_R(t)) was superseded by step-106's quadruple, despite step-107's otherwise-correct attribution of the quadruple to step-106.

rows.anchor: Three incompatible bindings of the E-scale, and three of the C-scale, with verdicts issued under the superseded bindings ... Scale proliferation, measured
rows.statement: TV-F-053 confirms by direct line-number citation the three incompatible E3 bindings (step-108 'automated test', step-109 'verification evidence', step-116 'behavioral evidence') and the three-way C0-C6/C1-C7 collision (steps 108/119/120), and states the measured scale-proliferation total: 49 distinct scales across the 101-120 band with zero explicit mappings between any pair.

rows.anchor: A FACT label is applied to an unevidenced assertion in the section defining what FACT means ... Thirteen existence assertions, zero evidence rows
rows.statement: Step-132 (current-state reconstruction) declares the band's mode switch from Design to Evidence, introducing a FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS/TARGET classification that is never mapped onto step-109's near-identical earlier Observed/Inferred/Specified/Claimed scale (that step is never cited); its own worked example applies the FACT label to an entirely unevidenced assertion ('.claude/ contains a memory directory') within the very section that defines what FACT means.

rows.anchor: 43 scales in 20 steps ≈ 2.15 new epistemic scales per step. Fourteen are used exactly once and never again. Zero crosswalks are published
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: 43 distinct epistemic/maturity/verdict scales are introduced across steps 121-140 (roughly 2.15 new scales per step), fourteen used exactly once, with zero published crosswalks between any pair, including four distinct four-valued epistemic scales (two within this band plus step-109's and step-124's) that all attempt the same job.

rows.anchor: Verdict codomain drift — five incompatible definitions, none superseding another ... GT-004 ... is untypable under 154, 156 and 157, because UNKNOWN is not in their codomains
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: the verification-verdict codomain drifts through five incompatible definitions across the band (145's PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, 151's FAIL/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, 154's six-value set dropping UNKNOWN, 156's INCONCLUSIVE-based four-value set, 157's two further variants), with no supersession recorded for any transition, leaving step-145's GT-004 invariant literally untypable under three of the five later codomains because its required UNKNOWN value no longer exists in them.

rows.anchor: Rules-live-once, systematically violated ... Approximately 169 invariant IDs are minted across the band in 15 families with zero cross-family references and zero deduplication
rows.statement: VJ-9: one rule (a governed action requires authorization) is independently minted seven times under seven different identifiers across seven files (KOS-ARCH-002, AF-002, GT-002, A-INV-003, IC-008, API-003, C-018/C-019/ARCH-AUTH-001) with none citing any other; similar five-way duplicate clusters exist for 'verification identifies exact rule version', 'projections must be rebuildable', and 'agent memory is not authoritative' -- roughly 169 invariant IDs total minted across 15 families in the band with zero cross-family references and zero deduplication.

rows.anchor: Class 1 — Same object, incompatible definitions ... K_t: 7+ incompatible tuple forms ... Zero: 9 signatures ... Eight distinct 'epistemic object' tuples
rows.statement: Class 1 of the AC register catalogues 16 same-object-incompatible-definition contradictions (C-001..016) in the pre-067 corpus: K_t has 7+ incompatible tuple arities none retracted; S_t has 4 arities; Zero has 9 signatures with a silently-varying third argument; DC(d)/EC tuples conflict 6-vs-7 and 2-/4-/9-tuple; eight distinct 'epistemic object' tuples with no mapping between any two; five uncertainty taxonomies (8/5/7/2/3-way) unreconciled; an Assessment-vs-Assertion vocabulary schism; two disjoint 'kernel' candidate sets (049's 8 primitives intersect 162's 7 kernel candidates at zero tokens); and two Policy signatures mutually uncited.

rows.anchor: Class 2 — Law-level conflicts ... Monotonicity: step-004 axiom vs demonstrated non-monotonicity ... Commutativity/associativity required ... vs denied universally with counterexample
rows.statement: Class 2 of the AC register catalogues 34 law-level contradictions (C-020..053) in the pre-067 corpus, including: a monotonicity axiom (S+(E union {e}) >= S+(E)) directly contradicted by a demonstrated non-monotone case (0.977->0.728) and a separate universal-refutation result, with the candidate scope-distinction that would resolve it left unstated in the corpus; commutativity/associativity required by one file and denied-with-counterexample by another, mutually uncited; idempotency required as a kernel invariant while resting on an evidence-identity notion the corpus itself marks Unresolved; a Lord/Sarathi role-reversal within one series (deciding authority flips between the two roles with no supersession); three silent formal regressions (Beta-Bernoulli reliability to qualitative, strong-Kleene tables to a status set with no connective semantics, a five-time temporal model to three times) none of which any file notes as a loss; and a mathematically invalid likelihood-ratio factorization (LR(E1,E2)=LR(E1)*LR(E2)) gated on only one of two required conditional-independence assumptions, producing a verified 10x overstatement of evidential support that propagates into two later files.

rows.anchor: Class 3 — Notation collisions ... 𝓔 (entity/evidence/events/status-set/input-space) ... No global symbol table exists anywhere in the corpus
rows.statement: Class 3 of the AC register documents corpus-wide glyph overloading as a systemic finding: at least twelve symbols (script-E, script-P, script-C, A, script-K, delta, alpha, Pi, H, T_tau, W_t, U) each carry between two and five unrelated meanings across the corpus, with H mixing hypothesis/entropy/history within a single expression in one file, and explicitly states no global symbol table exists anywhere in the corpus; also catalogues undefined symbols appearing inside results the corpus itself labels 'frozen'/load-bearing.

rows.anchor: Class 4 — Phase-2B ... step-002 §5 defines e1≺e2 ... §6 Case B uses the reverse ... two overlapping transition-operation alphabets over the same carrier K, same day
rows.statement: Class 4 (Phase-2B, steps 001-010 deep read) finds: a precedence-relation orientation (e1<e2) defined one way at its birth section and used in the opposite orientation two sections later in the same file, never fixed anywhere in steps 001-010; two overlapping 8/9-operation transition alphabets minted the same day over the same carrier with no reconciliation, later joined by a third partially-overlapping event set; and a systemic invariant-namespace collision affecting every bare single-letter invariant ID (A, U, S, C, T, I, D) traced back to the corpus's first 25 steps, established as the origin of a pattern that recurs through the later step-158-region registry chaos.

rows.anchor: Class 5 — Phase-2C 025-series ... Zero has ten unreconciled definitions corpus-wide ... Lord/Sārathi roles reversed within the 025-series ... Three silent formal regressions
rows.statement: Class 5 (025-series deep verification) finds Zero accumulates ten unreconciled definitions corpus-wide (five carried from Class 4 plus four more minted inside one single file); a status set declared with 9 values but used with 11 and never re-closed, with one predicate name simultaneously used as an element, a set-function, and a predicate (ill-typed); a Lord/Sarathi decision-authority reversal within the 025-series itself with no supersession act; a second confirmed mathematically-invalid likelihood-factorization instance (same defect class as C-067, independently occurring); an evidence-tuple schism (a 10-field epistemic tuple vs an unrelated 8-field cryptographic tuple sharing one symbol); and a closure claim over a state space that is never actually constructed, rendering it unfalsifiable as stated.

rows.anchor: Per the anti-reconciliation procedure ... such resolutions are PROPOSED REFINEMENTS, never existing theory
rows.statement: States the register's standing methodological rule: even where a Class-1 contradiction looks resolvable by adding a scoping distinction (e.g. a proviso that would reconcile the monotonicity axiom with its counterexample), such a resolution is recorded strictly as a PROPOSED REFINEMENT and never treated as existing theory -- the final-theory work must trace provenance, test supersession, and classify each variant as equivalent/compatible/incompatible/orthogonal before any reconciliation is accepted.

rows.anchor: the corpus's only measure-theoretic content sits in an unnumbered orphan that no numbered step consumes ... the single largest scope failure in the batch
rows.statement: The unnumbered orphan file preceding Step 186 introduces the corpus's only measure-theoretic apparatus (Dirac observation streams, an evidence measure space, Dempster-Shafer belief/plausibility, a Reconstruction Theorem candidate carefully hedged as 'recorded epistemic trajectory' not 'actual historical reality'), but its evidence measure mu_E is silently a measure on the time-index, not on the evidence set it claims to measure (ill-typed); every one of these constructs is abandoned by silence within one step (Step 186), with no rejection recorded, in a corpus directory literally named 'phase_measure_theory'.

rows.anchor: VL-1 ... VL-15 ... Semantic elevation governed, semantic demotion ungoverned ... STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY, not merely an omission
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: catalogues 15 numbered intra-scope contradictions (VL-1 through VL-15) across steps 186-205, most severely the filtration-vs-entropy-growth conflict, a partial order asserted then drawn as a total order, four incompatible bindings of the Proposition/K_t/T_tau symbols within single files, the 201-A freeze's undisclosed omission of Policy from its own derivation basis, a reversed Observation-Evidence containment relation, and the structural semantic-elevation/demotion asymmetry (VL-13) identified as the freeze audit's central finding.

rows.anchor: VK-16 — I_1..I_5 five-for-five ID collision ... A reader encountering 'I_3' in this corpus cannot determine which proposition is meant
rows.statement: Step-171 mints a five-invariant registry (I_1..I_5) that collides index-for-index and content-for-content with Step-161's already-existing I_1..I_5, both explicitly framed as candidate constitutional articles, with zero acknowledgement in either direction, rendering any bare 'I_n' citation in the corpus ambiguous.

rows.anchor: Cross-cutting pattern — INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION WITHOUT CITATION ... Unknown ≠ False: seven times
rows.statement: Batch-level pattern: several results are independently re-derived without citation multiple times across the 28-file band -- State-does-not-contain-History three times, Capability!=Authority four times, Unknown!=False seven times, evidence non-independence three times, and the four-relation actor model twice -- none of the repeated derivations citing any of the prior ones.

rows.anchor: FIVE in-scope I-registries + six prior-corpus registries in one namespace ... one back-reference in 28 files, and it is fictional
rows.statement: Batch-level finding: across steps 158-185 five separate in-scope invariant registries (161, 162, 171, 185, plus 162's own unnumbered addition) compete with six prior-corpus registries occupying the same I-namespace, producing two six-for-six and one five-for-five content collisions with zero crosswalks; the only invariant back-reference in all 28 files occurs inside a hypothetical imagined AI utterance, not as a genuine citation.

rows.anchor: The phase is named after mathematics that no numbered step contains ... NOT ONE contains σ-algebra, measurable space, measure space, or Lebesgue ... the single most consequential finding of the verification to date
rows.statement: TV-F-062 (CRITICAL, rated the single most consequential finding of the verification programme to date): a first-hand corpus-wide grep across all 473 files finds zero of the 215 numbered steps contain sigma-algebra, measurable space, measure space, or Lebesgue -- every occurrence sits in four pre-Step-001 research files dated one day before the corpus began, plus the unnumbered orphan; the nearest substitute (Dempster-Shafer belief functions) appears in 22 files but only through step-027 of 215, after which it disappears from the numbered corpus entirely with no recorded rejection or supersession, taking with it the only formalism in which Zero's central property (Unknown!=False) was actually derivable.

rows.anchor: Step 200, the sole whole-system falsification pass, cannot fail ... By the corpus's own I_47 ... none of these labels may be read as verification
rows.statement: TV-F-063 restates and sharpens the Step-200 finding: its 25-query coherence test cannot fail by construction (representability is not coherence), and its own correctly-hedged 'Provisional Coherence Proposition' self-limitation is then violated 17 times by unqualified verdict labels across four subsequent files (200/202/204/205), all of which the corpus's own invariant I_47 (governance approval must not silently upgrade epistemic strength) would disqualify as verification.

rows.anchor: The Step-201 fork is unadjudicated, and the half demanding real testing is orphaned ... The fork was resolved by silence in favour of the half that froze the vocabulary, and against the half that would have tested it
rows.statement: TV-F-064 confirms by grep that Step 201-B's 80-step adversarial/statistical/property-based-testing programme has zero successors in steps 202-205, while 201-A's vocabulary freeze captures the entire successor chain -- the fork is resolved by silence in favor of the less epistemically honest half (201-B explicitly states PROVISIONALLY COHERENT != PROVEN != FINAL, a distinction the successor chain does not carry forward).

rows.anchor: ROOT CAUSE — a structural asymmetry, not an oversight ... One missing dual invariant explains all of them
rows.statement: TV-F-065 identifies the root cause of the vocabulary freeze's silent term deletions (Witness, Determination, Conflict-as-object) as a structural asymmetry in the invariant registry: I_73/196.54 governs only implicit semantic elevation, and no invariant anywhere in the I_21-I_75 registry governs implicit semantic demotion -- this single missing dual invariant is shown to explain every silent drop in the corpus, not just the freeze (five terms dropped before Step 186, Zero at 186->187, three at the freeze, Ambiguous/Candidate at 203.6).

rows.anchor: 93% of the invariant registry is write-only ... a dead registry, never retired
rows.statement: TV-F-066 measures that of the 55 invariants in the contiguous, collision-free I_21-I_75 registry, only 4 (I_34, I_47, I_70, I_73) are ever cited again after being issued, and two of those four are the same rule under different numbers -- approximately 93% of the registry is write-only; separately notes the ten axioms M1-M10 are declared once and cited zero times, with M6 and M7 silently violated by the freeze and the registry never formally retired.

rows.anchor: Twelve intra-band contradictions, four of them mathematical ... The arithmetic 10×8×6×7×5 = 16,800 is correct; its inputs contradict the file's own enumerations by a factor of ~23
rows.statement: TV-F-067 consolidates the batch's twelve intra-band contradictions, isolating four with genuine mathematical content (the filtration-vs-entropy-growth conflict violating the tower property, a partial order argued then drawn as a total order, Step 203's state-cardinality arithmetic being correct but its inputs contradicting the same file's own enumerations by a factor of about 23, and a commutativity claim false under the architecture's own lineage-bearing state model) plus a fifth self-refutation (an invariant demanding statistical-method provenance violated by an unnamed confidence-interval method two sections earlier in the same file).

rows.anchor: Eight graphs, three registries, seven relation vocabularies, none closed ... Transition validity is defined six times ... Conservation names four distinct relations
rows.statement: TV-F-068 measures the batch's operator/registry drift precisely: eight distinct named graphs collapse into three incompatible registries with no closure; transition validity is defined with six different arities across six sections, none citing another; the word 'conservation' is used for four genuinely distinct mathematical relations (set inclusion twice, exact set accumulation, and equality); and seven relation-type vocabularies coexist with no computed pairwise overlap and no successor citing a predecessor.

rows.anchor: Zero executions across 259 code fences ... This continues the corpus-wide pattern without exception: across the ~120 documents deep-verified so far, zero empirical acts
rows.statement: TV-F-069 confirms zero execution markers across 259 code fences in 22 files (all text/ASCII), with only three arithmetically-checkable computations in the entire band, all independently verified (one correct-but-fabricated-inputs, one correct-but-vacuous-telescoping, one correct-but-method-unspecified); states that across roughly 120 corpus documents deep-verified by this point in the overall verification programme, the finding of zero empirical acts holds without a single exception.

rows.anchor: Steps 202–205 each cite only their immediate predecessor and nothing they displace ... a reader cannot reconstruct why the prior conclusions were abandoned
rows.statement: TV-F-070 confirms each of steps 202-205 cites only its immediate chain predecessor and is silent on everything it displaces or reproduces (202 silent on the relation vocabularies it replaces, 203 silent on the identical prior result it answers, 204 silent on verbatim-reproducing step 198, 205 silent on Step 165's directly comparable and mostly-deleted aggregate table); notes the aggravating fact that the individual conclusions of 202-205 are largely sound architectural work, so the defect is provenance-reconstructability, not correctness -- by the corpus's own external-architect reconstructability test (from Step 201-B), the answer for this segment is no.

rows.anchor: What survives from this band ... The corpus's own most accurate self-assessments are 200.47 and 201-B's PROVISIONALLY COHERENT ≠ PROVEN ≠ FINAL. Both are correct, and both are contradicted by the verdict labels the corpus then issues
rows.statement: Closing summary for steps 186-205: lists the verifier-endorsed survivors (EpistemicState-non-monotonic/Lineage-monotonic as the band's most-reused correct result, Kernel-enforces-not-originates-authority, EpistemicStrength!=GovernanceStatus, the scalar-confidence-insufficiency impossibility argument, SystemHistory-subset-of-RealityHistory as the band's last and one of its best invariants, and invariant-driven aggregate derivation as a method); characterizes the band's overall posture as distinctions sound and sharp, formalizations named rather than constructed, tests narrated rather than run, and the corpus's own most accurate self-assessments of its epistemic status being simultaneously correct and contradicted by its own subsequent verdict labels.

rows.anchor: Step 180 forbids Confirmed and then declares five Confirmed bounded contexts one section later ... the sentence committing it invokes the very discipline it breaks as its justification
rows.statement: TV-F-071 pinpoints the fabricated bounded-context promotion (Step 180) with more precision than the original band report: the promotion to '5 Confirmed BCs' occurs in the section immediately following the file's own explicit boxed prohibition against exactly that ('not: ConfirmedBoundary'), and the sentence committing the violation cites the discipline it just broke as its own justification.

rows.anchor: three products over unscaled quantities, in three separate bands, none noticing the others
rows.statement: TV-F-072 cross-references Step-184's dimensionally-incoherent EpistemicDebt=Importance*Recoverability*Missingness formula against two independently-occurring instances of the identical defect class (a product of unscaled quantities with no established scale type) in two other verification bands: step-206's weighted boundary score and step-124's ActionRisk=Impact*Irreversibility*Scope -- three separate authors/steps committing the same measurement-theory error with none aware of the others.

rows.anchor: Fifteen invariant registries minted in 28 files, zero crosswalks, one back-reference — and it is fictional ... Every registry in this band is a second copy of something that already existed
rows.statement: TV-F-073 enumerates all fifteen ID registries minted across steps 158-185 with zero crosswalks between any pair and confirms the single back-reference across all 28 files (Step 164's 'invariant I-07') occurs inside a hypothetical AI utterance rather than a genuine citation; confirms Canonical Discovery was never performed by verifying the absence of all six pre-existing corpus registries (E-K1-10, INV-1-20, I1-I20, C1-C7, GT/GG/GE/GC/GA, the 8-primitive kernel) from all 28 files.

rows.anchor: the terminal high-support state is called CONFIRMED ... Established ... and Determined ... the single clearest ubiquitous-language defect in the band
rows.statement: TV-F-074 identifies the sharpest single UL defect in the band: two steps (183, 185) use 'Determined' as the name of the terminal high-support Knowledge status value, making it homonymous with the separate domain aggregate 'Determination' owned by a distinct bounded context -- inside the very corpus whose constitutional invariants include Determination!=Decision and Evidence!=Knowledge.

rows.anchor: A genuine mathematical error at 167.32, correctly repaired eight steps later without anyone noticing
rows.statement: TV-F-076 frames the Step-167 mutual-information error and its Step-175 repair as one continuous finding: the false strict inequality I(S;H)<H(H) is silently corrected eight steps later by Step 175's proper non-injectivity argument, with no citation, no correction notice, and no indication the author recognized the connection -- under the first-invalid-inference rule, everything downstream of the original error remains conditional on this uncredited repair.

rows.anchor: Against ~1,600 self-confirming experiments verified so far, this band contains the corpus's only real adversarial testing ... the band agent corrected its own brief, and the correction is sound
rows.statement: TV-F-077 states that against approximately 1,600 self-confirming experiments verified across the corpus to date, steps 158-185 contain the only four genuine adversarial falsification passes found so far (169, 175, 178, 181), and explicitly endorses the band agent's self-correction of its own commissioning brief (Step 172 reclassified from expected-genuine-falsification to narrated-pass; Step 181 added to the genuine set instead) as sound.

rows.anchor: Step 158's reality test: specified, commissioned, never performed ... presented as the output of the experiment that was never executed, with the pass criterion neither evaluated nor waived
rows.statement: TV-F-078 (CRITICAL) confirms Step 158's reality test was specified and commissioned but never performed across all 28 files (zero repository inspection, zero shell invocations, one mathematical reproducible witness), and highlights Step 185 as the sharpest recurrence of the same failure mode: an executable test with an explicit maturity-gate pass criterion is designed, never run, and six constitutional invariants are shipped anyway presented as if they were the experiment's output.

rows.anchor: Overall: a coherent, largely well-reasoned, entirely unexecuted architectural monologue. Its worst defects are not reasoning errors but bookkeeping failures
rows.statement: Closing summary for steps 158-185 lists the band's verifier-endorsed survivors (168.57's multi-dimensional state, Step 175's identifiability proof as the corpus's only reproducible witness, Step 184's three protected transitions as the most implementable AI-safety result in the corpus, Step 185's bitemporality, Step 166's AgentSession!=BusinessProcess, Step 182's question-decomposition and type-system-scoping results, and Step 173's treatment of the platform's own name as an architectural risk) and characterizes the band's defects as bookkeeping failures (fifteen uncrosswalked registries, six definitions of K, eight meanings of I, one unlicensed epistemic promotion) rather than reasoning errors.

rows.anchor: One executable invariant exists in 473 files: I_Dependency ... It proves the corpus's own methodology can produce definitions — which makes the named-only status of the other ~500 a choice, not a limitation
rows.statement: States the corpus-wide invariant census: roughly 500+ invariant IDs minted across roughly 25 registries with zero published crosswalks, of which exactly one (I_Dependency) is genuinely a decidable predicate over named objects, framed as proof the corpus's own methodology is capable of producing real definitions, making the named-only status of the remaining ~500 a demonstrated choice rather than a limitation.

rows.anchor: The kernel (§10) is NOT resolved ... NO CANONICAL FORM ESTABLISHED remains the correct verdict; no sense may be selected for elegance
rows.statement: States the kernel question remains unresolved with at least five distinct competing senses (mathematical primitive, epistemic, DDD shared kernel, architectural tier, implementation substrate) plus a sixth internal triple-sense collision within a single step (070), and that 'NO CANONICAL FORM ESTABLISHED' is affirmed as the correct verdict, explicitly forbidding selection of any sense for aesthetic reasons.

rows.anchor: Four of the six files in the entire corpus that contain measure-theoretic vocabulary are in this pre-step cluster ... The measure theory the phase is named after lives here, before Step 001, and never enters the numbered sequence
rows.statement: Locates the corpus's measure-theoretic content precisely: four of the six total files containing measure-theory vocabulary sit in the pre-Step-001 research cluster (Era 0), confirming (independent of the later corpus-wide grep in TV-F-062) that the phase's namesake mathematics lives entirely before the numbered step sequence begins.

rows.anchor: SemanticDemotionGoverned is the only atom in the core with no corpus source ... One missing dual invariant explains every abandonment this programme has found
rows.statement: Identifies a sixth finding that is a structural gap rather than a conflict: no invariant in any of the roughly 25 registries governs semantic demotion (only elevation is governed, via I_73/196.54), making every silent deletion in the corpus formally permissible -- unifying seven previously separately-found abandonment incidents (the 201-A freeze's term deletions, Zero's drop, Ambiguous/Candidate's drop, the Golden Trace apparatus, the C1-C7 constitution, Dempster-Shafer, and measure theory itself) under one missing dual invariant, called a stronger and more useful result than cataloguing the abandonments individually.

lexical.anchor: §32.34 ... immediately self-invalidated at §32.34's own next line ... §32.79 ... a fourth competing spine object

governance.anchor: If the corpus contains K_t = A and later K_t = B, do not simply choose B ... The output may legitimately be: NO CANONICAL FORM ESTABLISHED. That is a valid verification result

rationale_evidence.anchor: §32.34 ... immediately self-invalidated at §32.34's own next line ... §32.79 ... a fourth competing spine object
rationale_evidence.statement: Step-032's Status(A) six-value enum is declared and then withdrawn as non-mutually-exclusive within the same section; its EpistemicClaim EC 11-tuple is identified as a fourth competing 'spine' object alongside step-031's 6-tuple assertion, 7-tuple K_t, and its own 5-tuple State(A); its Belnap-FOUR-equivalent lattice claim is neither named nor cited as Belnap's bilattice, and no join/meet operation is ever defined.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge-state spine — five incompatible variants, none designated canonical, no migration ever noted ... Total: 30+ tuples. Not one has a single typed component
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: the corpus's central knowledge-state tuple has five incompatible variants across steps 026-040 (8, 9, 10+open, 7, and 11 elements respectively), with the version actually used downstream (step-031's 7-tuple) dropping Uncertainty, TemporalState and Arguments; over 30 distinct tuples are catalogued scope-wide and not one has a single typed component (no codomain, cardinality, or optionality declared for any element), which the meta-file's own M1 (Type correctness) criterion would fail for all 30 -- offered as one reason M1 was never applied.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Operator signature drift ... U(H) ... Decide/Decision ... Authorize/Admissible ... Authority ... Cost(I) ... Consistent ... Contradiction ... denotes ... Sensitivity ... Health/Meta vector ... Conflict lifecycle ... Drift family
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: twelve named operators/relations undergo unflagged signature drift across steps 026-040 (arity changes, domain changes, relation-to-function promotions, vector-to-scalar or vector-to-Boolean collapses), catalogued individually as items 1-12 including U(H), Decide, Authorize/Admissible, Authority, Cost(I), Consistent, Contradiction, denotes, Sensitivity, the Health/Meta vector, the conflict-state lifecycle, and the drift-kind family.

rationale_evidence.anchor: the only numbered identifier families anywhere in the 17 files are M1–M7 ... and P35.1–P35.7 ... Fourteen IDs total across 17 files and ~350 boxed statements ... Eleven overloaded symbols
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: across 17 files and roughly 350 boxed principles, only 14 statements ever receive a stable citable identifier (M1-M7, P35.1-P35.7), meaning nearly every load-bearing result is unciteable and gets re-stated (and thereby mutated) rather than re-used by later steps -- identified as the mechanism producing the tuple and signature drift; separately catalogues eleven overloaded bare-letter symbols (E, V, C, R, A, T, I, U, script-P, script-V) each denoting two or more different objects within the scope, five overlapping *Status/*State enums with no shared discipline, three independently-coined 'debt' concepts, and seven distinct uncertainty taxonomies.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 64 minted names, 63 unique. Genuinely defined: 1 ... 62 FAIL ... hinging on the undefined qualifiers silently (21) and material (14)
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level invariant census: 64 I_* names minted across the 16 files (63 unique, 1 exact duplicate), of which only I_Dependency passes a strict 'definition or merely a name' test; the dominant failure mode is an undefined modal qualifier, with 21 of 62 failing invariants turning on 'silently' and 14 on 'material', neither ever defined anywhere in the 16-file scope.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Three families drift without supersession notes: the kernel ... the Agent ... the Decision
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: three object families drift across steps 067-082 with no supersession note -- the kernel tuple (4 variants, arities 8/7/7+3/8), the Agent tuple (3 variants, arities 7/5/6), and the Decision function/tuple (6 signatures, arities ranging 4-11) -- cataloguing 34 total tuple/state-object variants in order of appearance.

Batch-level finding: twelve symbols (I, M, P, A, S, C, theta, U, e, !=, +, ~) each carry between two and six distinct senses across steps 067-082, with '!=' itself flagged as carrying a normative ('should not be conflated') sense in most occurrences despite being the corpus's single most-used operator, never disambiguated.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Five D, four S, two 𝒦 ... Step 100 reconciles none and introduces a memberless sixth S_t
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: across steps 083-100 the corpus carries five incompatible Decision-object definitions, four incompatible system-state tuples, and two incompatible kernel-state tuples (K and K_t), none reconciled by step-100's closure claim, which additionally introduces a seventh, memberless S_t.

rationale_evidence.anchor: ~175 invariants minted ... 0 of ~175 are definitions ... 'material' (appears in 61 invariant texts)
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level invariant census for steps 083-100: ~175 I_* names minted, 0 pass the definition test, with the hedge word 'material' alone appearing in 61 of the invariant texts as an unbound, undefined quantifier; at least 9 names collide with the 067-082 invariant families and several near-duplicate invariant families exist for single ideas (graceful degradation, cache freshness, criticality-proportional effort, constrained optimization, correlated evidence).

rationale_evidence.anchor: 49 catalogued scales ... Does any file map one scale onto another? No — zero explicit mappings exist in the 20 files
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: 49 distinct epistemic-status/evidence/verdict scales are introduced across steps 101-120 with zero explicit mappings between any pair of them; three fatal symbol collisions are isolated -- E-scale bound three incompatible ways (108/109/116), C-scale bound three incompatible ways (108/119/120), and F/F1 bound to unrelated concepts within step-120 alone.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 43 scales in 20 steps ≈ 2.15 new epistemic scales per step. Fourteen are used exactly once and never again. Zero crosswalks are published
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: 43 distinct epistemic/maturity/verdict scales are introduced across steps 121-140 (roughly 2.15 new scales per step), fourteen used exactly once, with zero published crosswalks between any pair, including four distinct four-valued epistemic scales (two within this band plus step-109's and step-124's) that all attempt the same job.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Verdict codomain drift — five incompatible definitions, none superseding another ... GT-004 ... is untypable under 154, 156 and 157, because UNKNOWN is not in their codomains
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level finding: the verification-verdict codomain drifts through five incompatible definitions across the band (145's PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, 151's FAIL/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, 154's six-value set dropping UNKNOWN, 156's INCONCLUSIVE-based four-value set, 157's two further variants), with no supersession recorded for any transition, leaving step-145's GT-004 invariant literally untypable under three of the five later codomains because its required UNKNOWN value no longer exists in them.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Rules-live-once, systematically violated ... Approximately 169 invariant IDs are minted across the band in 15 families with zero cross-family references and zero deduplication
rationale_evidence.statement: VJ-9: one rule (a governed action requires authorization) is independently minted seven times under seven different identifiers across seven files (KOS-ARCH-002, AF-002, GT-002, A-INV-003, IC-008, API-003, C-018/C-019/ARCH-AUTH-001) with none citing any other; similar five-way duplicate clusters exist for 'verification identifies exact rule version', 'projections must be rebuildable', and 'agent memory is not authoritative' -- roughly 169 invariant IDs total minted across 15 families in the band with zero cross-family references and zero deduplication.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Class 3 — Notation collisions ... 𝓔 (entity/evidence/events/status-set/input-space) ... No global symbol table exists anywhere in the corpus
rationale_evidence.statement: Class 3 of the AC register documents corpus-wide glyph overloading as a systemic finding: at least twelve symbols (script-E, script-P, script-C, A, script-K, delta, alpha, Pi, H, T_tau, W_t, U) each carry between two and five unrelated meanings across the corpus, with H mixing hypothesis/entropy/history within a single expression in one file, and explicitly states no global symbol table exists anywhere in the corpus; also catalogues undefined symbols appearing inside results the corpus itself labels 'frozen'/load-bearing.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Cross-cutting pattern — INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION WITHOUT CITATION ... Unknown ≠ False: seven times
rationale_evidence.statement: Batch-level pattern: several results are independently re-derived without citation multiple times across the 28-file band -- State-does-not-contain-History three times, Capability!=Authority four times, Unknown!=False seven times, evidence non-independence three times, and the four-relation actor model twice -- none of the repeated derivations citing any of the prior ones.

sources.note: Five-stage Generation->Assessment->Selection->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution architecture extracted from a biological 'millions-to-one' metaphor, with Selection redefined as set-valued (not single-winner), selection-bias/winner's-curse risk, and Selection Evidence != Validation Evidence; names and motivates the KR-M2O-2026-09-02 experiment.

rows.anchor: Claim A: 'Knowledge = one selected proposal.' Reject. ... A selected hypothesis can be false. This is exactly the unresolved factivity problem. So: P* = Select(𝓗) does not imply: Knows(P*). At most: Accepted(P*).
rows.statement: Rejects Claim A ('Knowledge = one selected proposal'): a selected hypothesis P*=Select(H) can be false, so selection implies at most Accepted(P*), not Knows(P*) -- directly tied to the still-unresolved factivity problem.

rows.anchor: Claim B: 'The field selects the best proposal.' Too strong. A selection function requires 𝓗, E, C, S but also a comparison/evaluation relation. ... We currently do not have the required ordering ⪰. So this is premature.
rows.statement: Rejects Claim B ('the field selects the best proposal') as premature: any 'best' selection presupposes a comparison/evaluation ordering (>=) that the theory does not yet have.

rows.anchor: Claim C: 'One candidate survives.' Also too strong. ... |𝒜_Q|=0 or |𝒜_Q|=1 or |𝒜_Q|>1. ... Million→One must become: Many Candidates → Admissible Candidate Set with cardinality: 0, 1, >1.
rows.statement: Rejects Claim C ('one candidate survives') citing the corpus's existing set-valued-determination work: the admissible candidate set A_Q may have cardinality 0, 1, or >1; 'Million->One' must become 'Many Candidates -> Admissible Candidate Set'.

rows.anchor: Claim D: 'Most hypotheses are false.' ... not a universal mathematical fact. It depends on the hypothesis-generation distribution. ... We should replace it with: Candidate generation may have a high failure rate. That is an empirical property of a generator, not a law of epistemology.
rows.statement: Rejects Claim D ('most hypotheses are false') as a universal law, replacing it with the weaker empirical claim 'candidate generation may have a high failure rate' -- a property of the specific generator, not a law of epistemology.

rows.anchor: 𝓗_t → Assessment_t → 𝒜_t → Transformation_t where 𝓗_t = candidate hypothesis space, Assessment_t = evaluation of candidates, 𝒜_t ⊆ 𝓗_t = surviving/admissible candidates, Transformation_t = construction of the resulting epistemic product/state.
rows.statement: Proposes the core four-stage abstraction Hypotheses_t -> Assessment_t -> AdmissibleCandidates_t (subset of Hypotheses_t) -> Transformation_t, judged significantly better than the biological 'millions of sperm -> one knowledge' framing.

rows.anchor: Select: 𝓗_Q × 𝒱_t → 𝒫(𝓗_Q) ... Select(𝓗_Q,E,S,C,M) = 𝒜_Q. Then: No admissible candidate |𝒜_Q|=0, Unique admissible candidate |𝒜_Q|=1, Multiple admissible candidates |𝒜_Q|>1.
rows.statement: Redefines Select as returning a subset (power-set-valued) of the hypothesis space rather than a single element: Select:H_Q x V_t -> P(H_Q), admitting zero, one, or multiple admissible candidates.

rows.anchor: ρ_t = 1 − |𝓗_{t+1}|/|𝓗_t|. This measures filtering, not knowledge gain. That distinction is critical.
rows.statement: Defines a Candidate Reduction rate rho_t=1-|H_{t+1}|/|H_t| as a measure of filtering, explicitly distinguished from knowledge gain -- reducing the candidate set is not the same as gaining knowledge.

rows.anchor: H_1 has stronger evidence but poorer explanatory power, while H_2 has stronger explanatory power but weaker evidence. Neither may dominate. Then: H_1 ⋡ H_2 and: H_2 ⋡ H_1. Therefore both survive: 𝒜_Q={H_1,H_2}. ... The Linga's Millions model has accidentally brought us directly to one of our existing theoretical bottlenecks [⪰].
rows.statement: Argues for a partial order over hypotheses rather than a scalar 'best' score: two hypotheses with incomparable strengths (H1 stronger evidence/weaker explanatory power, H2 vice versa) neither dominates the other under a partial order, so both survive in the admissible set -- directly implicating the still-undefined epistemic-status ordering (>=) as this document's central bottleneck too.

rows.anchor: Selection(𝓗,E,S) [answers] Which candidates survive the evaluation rule? [versus] Determination(Q,E,S) [answers] What does the available epistemic state warrant as an answer to this inquiry? Those can differ. ... Candidate reduction ≠ Determination.
rows.statement: Establishes Selection != Determination as a hard DDD boundary: Selection asks which candidates survive an evaluation rule, Determination asks what the epistemic state warrants as an answer to the inquiry; successfully reducing 100 hypotheses to 2 (Selection succeeding) is compatible with Determination(Q) being unable to determine uniquely.

rows.anchor: Even if 𝒜_Q={H_1} we still have: Determined(H_1) but cannot automatically conclude: Knows(H_1). ... Generation → Assessment → Selection → Determination → Knowledge Attribution with each arrow representing a different responsibility.
rows.statement: Extends the responsibility chain to five distinct stages: Generation->Assessment->Selection->Determination->KnowledgeAttribution, noting even a uniquely determined hypothesis (Determined(H_1)) does not automatically give Knows(H_1) -- the unresolved factivity mechanism still gates the final step.

rows.anchor: If you generate millions of hypotheses and then select the strongest-performing one, you can get max_i Score(H_i) that looks impressive even when all candidates are noise. This is the statistical phenomenon of selection / multiple comparisons / winner's curse. So: Best observed candidate ≠ Best underlying hypothesis.
rows.statement: Introduces the statistical selection-bias/multiple-comparisons/winner's-curse phenomenon into KnowledgeOS: selecting the best-scoring candidate from a large generated set can look impressive even when all candidates are pure noise, establishing 'best observed candidate != best underlying hypothesis' -- directly relevant to AI systems generating thousands of candidate explanations and picking the best apparent fit (best overfit).

rows.anchor: Selection must be separated from validation. ... 𝓗 → Screening → Candidate Set → Validation → Determination. ... validation must include out-of-sample/independent evidence where applicable.
rows.statement: States the strong requirement 'Selection must be separated from Validation', restructuring the funnel into Hypotheses->Screening->CandidateSet->Validation->Determination, with validation requiring out-of-sample/independent evidence where applicable, connecting to the corpus's prior Freedman/Good/Bayesian/Dretske statistical work.

rows.anchor: H* = argmax_H S_train(H) does not imply: H* = argmax_H S_future(H). Therefore KnowledgeOS should distinguish: Selection Evidence ≠ Validation Evidence.
rows.statement: Formalizes the anti-overfitting principle: the hypothesis maximizing training-evidence score need not maximize future/validation-evidence score, giving the architectural distinction Selection Evidence != Validation Evidence.

rows.anchor: KR-M2O-2026-09-02 -- Candidate Multiplicity and Selection. Test: Generate N hypotheses. Vary N: 1,10,100,1000,10000. Apply identical evidence. Measure: candidate reduction, unique determination rate, false-selection rate, validation failure rate, hypothesis diversity, dependence between candidates. ... H0: More candidate generation does not necessarily improve epistemic quality. I strongly suspect this will survive.
rows.statement: Proposes the KR-M2O-2026-09-02 experiment: generate N hypotheses across N in {1,10,100,1000,10000} under identical evidence, measuring candidate reduction/unique-determination-rate/false-selection-rate/validation-failure-rate/diversity/dependence, comparing scalar/partial-order/threshold/Bayesian/Pareto selection methods, testing the adversarial null hypothesis that more candidate generation does not necessarily improve epistemic quality (predicted to survive).

experiment.hypothesis: More candidate generation does not necessarily improve epistemic quality (H0, expected to survive)
experiment.setup: generate N candidate hypotheses for N in {1,10,100,1000,10000} under identical evidence
experiment.assumptions: a selection method (scalar ranking, partial-order, threshold, Bayesian posterior, or Pareto) is applied consistently
experiment.inputs: N hypotheses plus fixed evidence set per trial
experiment.method: compute candidate reduction, unique-determination rate, false-selection rate, validation-failure rate, hypothesis diversity, and inter-candidate dependence across N and across selection methods
experiment.result: not run in this file; see S2462/P-candidate-multiplicity-and-selection.md

rows.anchor: Candidate Multiplicity is not a nuisance; it is a mathematical dimension of epistemic systems. ... generation → competition → assessment → selection → validation → determination → attribution. That is a genuine candidate extension of the theory. But I would not amend Theory v1.2 yet. First run the candidate-multiplicity experiment.
rows.statement: States the overall conclusion: candidate multiplicity is a genuine mathematical dimension of epistemic systems (not a nuisance), extending the theory's pipeline to generation->competition->assessment->selection->validation->determination->attribution; explicitly defers amending Theory v1.2 until the candidate-multiplicity experiment is run, with the decisive question being whether Selection/Assessment/CandidateSet introduce any irreducible capability beyond what the existing kernel-reduction experiments already derive.

rows.anchor: G_t: K_t,Q_t → 𝓗_t [Generation] ... A_t:(𝓗_t,E_t,M_t,S_t,C_t)→𝒱_t [Assessment] ... S_t:(𝓗_t,𝒱_t)→𝒜_t [Selection] ... D_t:(𝒜_t,Q_t)→𝒟_t [Determination] ... Γ_t:(𝒟_t,E_t,factivity policy)→K_t^attrib [Knowledge attribution].
rows.statement: Assembles a five-function architecture with explicit type signatures: Generation G_t(K_t,Q_t)->H_t, Assessment A_t(H_t,E_t,M_t,S_t,C_t)->V_t, Selection S_t(H_t,V_t)->A_t, Determination D_t(A_t,Q_t)->D_t, and Knowledge Attribution Gamma_t(D_t,E_t,factivity policy)->K_t^attrib -- substantially more rigorous than the source document's single K_new=Transform(Select(Millions,E,C,S),Y).

rows.anchor: H1: Increasing the number of generated candidates does not necessarily improve epistemic quality. ... H8: 'Best candidate' requires an ordering/comparison criterion. ... H9: Increasing candidate count can increase selection bias, overfitting, or false-selection risk. ... H12: The biological 'million-to-one' ratio has no universal epistemological status merely because the biological process has that property.
rows.statement: States the full twelve-hypothesis test matrix H1-H12: more candidates does not necessarily improve quality (H1); candidate reduction != progress (H2); selection != validation (H3); selection != determination (H4); a unique surviving candidate does not automatically imply Knowledge (H5); multiple survivors can be correct (H6); zero survivors can be correct (H7); 'best candidate' requires an ordering, not an assumed total ranking (H8); more candidates can increase selection bias/overfitting (H9); generation/assessment/selection/validation/determination/attribution may be separate responsibilities (H10); if existing operations reproduce all behavior, no new kernel primitive is justified (H11); the biological million-to-one ratio has no automatic epistemological status (H12).

rows.anchor: Candidate != Assessment, Assessment != Selection, Selection != Validation, Validation != Determination, Determination != Knowledge, Candidate count != Knowledge quantity, Candidate count != Knowledge quality, Candidate reduction != Epistemic progress, Acceptance != Truth, Survival != Factivity, Ranking != Validation, Fit != Causal validity, Evidence != Assessment, Credence != Truth, Knowledge != Epistemic State, Zero != Selection, Zero != Evaluation, Zero != State transformation.
rows.statement: Mandates preserving eighteen distinctions throughout the experiment (Candidate/Assessment/Selection/Validation/Determination/Knowledge chain, plus Acceptance!=Truth, Survival!=Factivity, Ranking!=Validation, Fit!=Causal validity, Credence!=Truth, Knowledge!=Epistemic State, and three Zero-is-not-X clauses), none to be collapsed for implementation convenience.

rows.anchor: Sel(H_t, V_t) -> A_t where A_t subseteq H_t. IMPORTANT: Selection MUST initially be set-valued. Possible outcomes: |A_t|=0, |A_t|=1, |A_t|>1. Do NOT define selection as argmax returning exactly one candidate.
rows.statement: Mandates Selection be implemented as strictly set-valued (Sel:H_t x V_t -> A_t subseteq H_t, admitting 0/1/>1 outcomes), forbidding an argmax-single-winner implementation from the start.

rows.anchor: First investigate whether a partial ordering is sufficient: H_i >= H_j ... Construct cases where: H_1 >= H_2 but not: H_2 >= H_1 and cases where neither dominates ... If incomparability occurs, preserve it. Do NOT force a winner. Only as a secondary experimental arm may you introduce: scalar ranking.
rows.statement: Mandates investigating partial ordering (H_i>=H_j) as the primary candidate-comparison mechanism before any scalar ranking, explicitly preserving incomparability where it occurs rather than forcing a winner; scalar ranking is permitted only as a secondary experimental arm with sensitivity analysis over weights/normalization/metric/count/dependence.

rows.anchor: ARM A -- SINGLE CANDIDATE n=1 ... ARM B n=10 ... ARM C n=100 ... ARM D n=1,000 ... ARM E n=10,000 ... If computationally reasonable, optionally: n=100,000 but do NOT sacrifice experimental validity merely to obtain a larger number.
rows.statement: Specifies five (optionally six) experimental arms varying candidate count n across 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 (optionally 100000), with the controlled-variation-in-n property prioritized over sheer scale.

rows.anchor: Construct synthetic worlds where evaluator-only ground truth is known. The agent/simulation MUST NOT have access to ground truth. At minimum create: 1. Unique true hypothesis ... 15. Selection-induced overfitting. ... Audit the simulator statically to ensure no truth leakage.
rows.statement: Requires 15 controlled synthetic epistemic worlds (unique true hypothesis; multiple observationally compatible hypotheses; no admissible hypothesis; one false-but-fitting hypothesis; multiple false hypotheses; correct-with-weak-evidence; false-with-strong-fit; model misspecification; dependent/independent/contradictory evidence; unobservable target; underdetermined target; temporal evidence conflict; selection-induced overfitting) with ground truth accessible only to the evaluator, never the epistemic agent, statically audited for truth leakage.

rows.anchor: G1: Random hypotheses ... G6: Generator containing a high proportion of false candidates. G7: Generator containing a high proportion of correct candidates. ... The statement 'Most hypotheses are false' must NOT be assumed. Measure the actual false proportion produced by each generator.
rows.statement: Requires seven distinct candidate generator types (random, diverse, correlated, near-duplicate, adversarial, high-false-proportion, high-correct-proportion) with the false-hypothesis proportion measured empirically per generator, never assumed a priori.

rows.anchor: Explicitly model candidate dependence. For example: H_1, H_2, H_3 may all originate from the same underlying assumption. Therefore: 3 candidates != 3 independent alternatives. Measure: candidate_dependence and distinguish: candidate diversity, candidate count.
rows.statement: Requires explicitly modeling and measuring candidate dependence, distinguishing candidate count from candidate diversity, since multiple candidates sharing an underlying assumption do not constitute independent alternatives.

rows.anchor: Construct a null world in which all candidate models have no real predictive advantage. Generate increasingly many candidates. Select the candidate with the best apparent training fit. ... Compare: training performance, validation performance, selection optimism. Test whether: max observed fit increases with candidate count while: held-out performance does not improve correspondingly.
rows.statement: Mandates a selection-bias/winner's-curse control test: in a null world where no candidate has real predictive advantage, generate increasing candidate counts, select by best apparent training fit, and compare training vs held-out (validation) performance -- testing whether max observed fit rises with candidate count while true held-out performance does not, directly testing 'more candidates => better knowledge'.

rows.anchor: CASE 1: 100 candidates -> 1 selected and determination is unique. CASE 2: 100 candidates -> 2 admissible candidates and determination is NOT unique. CASE 3: 100 candidates -> 0 admissible candidates and determination is impossible. The system MUST NOT force all three into a single 'winner' state.
rows.statement: Requires three explicit selection-vs-determination test cases (100 candidates yielding 1/2/0 admissible outcomes respectively) that must not be forced into a uniform single-winner representation.

rows.anchor: NC1: One candidate, false. ... NC8: Best training fit loses validation. NC9: Candidate count increases but epistemic gap remains constant. NC10: Candidate count decreases but gap increases. NC11: Selection produces one candidate but factivity remains unresolved. NC12: Scalar score forces a winner while partial ordering preserves incomparability. ... NC14: Generator produces mostly false candidates.
rows.statement: Specifies 14 required negative controls (NC1-NC14) covering false single candidates, absent true candidates among many, multiple admissible candidates, observationally equivalent candidates, evidence-correlation variations, training-fit-loses-validation, count-vs-gap decoupling in both directions, factivity-remaining-unresolved-despite-unique-selection, and scalar-vs-partial-order divergence.

rows.anchor: Can the entire candidate-generation/selection behaviour be represented using existing KnowledgeOS capabilities? ... Do NOT assume Select is primitive merely because the model uses the word 'selection.' Test derivability. For example: Selection may be derivable from Discriminate + Validate + Determine or it may require an irreducible capability.
rows.statement: Requires testing whether the candidate-generation/selection behavior is derivable from existing KnowledgeOS operators (Observe, Interpret, Represent, Relate, Discriminate, Hypothesize, Challenge, Validate, Revise, Determine, Select), explicitly forbidding assuming Select is primitive merely from its name; likewise tests CandidateSet, Ranking, Admissibility, Filtering, Competition for derivability.

rows.anchor: A. Redundancy: Selection = f(Discriminate,Validate,Determine). Then no new kernel capability. B. Independent domain responsibility but not kernel primitive: Selection is semantically distinct in DDD, but computationally derivable. C. Irreducible epistemic capability: No existing kernel operation can reproduce selection semantics ... Only C would give us a serious reason to reopen the kernel question.
rows.statement: Frames the decisive three-way outcome for the Selection capability: (A) Redundancy -- fully derivable from existing operators, no new kernel capability; (B) an independent DDD responsibility that remains computationally derivable; (C) an irreducible epistemic capability requiring no existing operator combination -- only outcome C would justify reopening the kernel question, and even then must not jump to a new canonical kernel given unresolved factivity/Contr/status-ordering/semantic-equivalence.

rows.anchor: DO NOT perform kernel minimality comparisons until semantic equivalence is adequately specified. ... this experiment may identify: candidate irreducible capability but may NOT claim: final minimal kernel unless the semantic-equivalence precondition is independently satisfied. If blocked, explicitly report: KERNEL MINIMALITY NOT TESTABLE.
rows.statement: Repeats the standing kernel-minimality-blocked rule: minimality comparisons are forbidden until semantic equivalence is adequately specified; the experiment may identify a candidate irreducible capability but must not claim a final minimal kernel, reporting 'KERNEL MINIMALITY NOT TESTABLE' if blocked.

rows.anchor: Ask: 'Under what conditions would the million-to-one model be unnecessary, false, useful, or genuinely structurally necessary?' The experiment must be capable of concluding: 'The model adds no new capability.' That is a successful result.
rows.statement: States the most important methodological principle: the experiment must ask under what conditions the million-to-one model would be unnecessary/false/useful/necessary, not how to force-fit it into KnowledgeOS; a conclusion of 'the model adds no new capability' is explicitly a successful, not a failed, result.

rows.anchor: NULL world: no candidate has any real predictive advantage. ... n=1 max training 0.0027, held-out 0.0030 ... n=10000 max training 0.6101, held-out −0.0120 ... selection optimism 0.6222 ... Apparent quality rises monotonically 0.00 → 0.61. Real quality never moves from zero. ... H1 confirmed. H9 confirmed.
rows.statement: [EXP]: in a null world where no candidate has real predictive advantage, apparent (training-fit) quality of the best-selected candidate rises monotonically from 0.00 (n=1) to 0.61 (n=10000) across 200 trials per arm, while the selected candidate's held-out performance remains statistically indistinguishable from zero at every n -- confirming H1 (more candidates does not improve quality) and H9 (more candidates increases selection bias), with the entire apparent gap attributable to selection optimism tracking the extreme-value bound sigma*sqrt(2 ln n)/sqrt(m).

experiment.hypothesis: H1 (more candidates does not improve epistemic quality) and H9 (more candidates increases selection bias)
experiment.setup: null world, no candidate has real predictive advantage; select best training fit; evaluate selected candidate on independent held-out draw; 200 trials per arm
experiment.assumptions: candidates and evidence generated under a null (no true signal) model
experiment.method: for each n, record max training score, held-out score of the selected candidate, held-out score averaged over all candidates, and selection optimism (difference)
experiment.result: max training rises 0.0027->0.6101; held-out (selected) stays near zero (-0.012 to 0.015); selection optimism rises 0.00->0.62, tracking sigma*sqrt(2 ln n)/sqrt(m)
experiment.interpretation: apparent quality improvement with more candidates is entirely selection optimism/winner's curse, not real epistemic gain
experiment.limitations: confined to the specific null-world simulation design
experiment.conclusion: [EXP] H1 and H9 confirmed

rows.anchor: §12 CASE 1 (100 candidates → unique determination) returned |A|=2, not 1. Rather than adjust the threshold, I computed why ... |A|=2 was the expected outcome, not a defect: it is the winner's curse reappearing in the determination arm.
